cards.explanation: The answer is Judah, friends. Verses 1 and 2 just read off the twelve names like a roll call. Then verse 3 slows way down: “The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah.” That's the list telling us which road it's taking.
The answer is wicked, friends. Verse 3 says Er, Judah's firstborn, “…was wicked in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD put him to death.” That's a heavy line. I think this one hurts.
The answer is Tamar, friends. Verse 4 says, “Tamar, Judah’s daughter-in-law, bore to him Perez and Zerah.” So the first three sons came by Bath-shua the Canaanite, and these two came by Tamar.
The answer is True, friends. Er, Onan and Shelah came by Bath-shua (verse 3), and Perez and Zerah came by Tamar. Verse 4 wraps it up: “Judah had five sons in all.” Three and two make five.

The answer is leader, friends. Verse 10 calls Nahshon “…a leader of the descendants of Judah.” Most names around him just get a quick "father of" and move on. Nahshon gets a title, and that earns him a little extra spotlight.

The answer is Boaz, friends. Verse 11 says “…Salmon was the father of Boaz.” This is the Boaz whose field Ruth, the Moabite (Ruth 1:22), went to glean in (Ruth 2:3). After a wall of names, a face you know feels like spotting a friend at a crowded family reunion.

The answer is Jesse, friends. Verse 12 says “…Obed was the father of Jesse.” And the list names seven sons of Jesse, with David at the end of that line. We just walked up to the front door of David's house.

The answer is David, friends. He's seventh and last on the list of Jesse's sons. Verse 15 finishes with “…and David seventh.” Seven names in order, and he's the one this whole list has been heading toward since Judah.
The answer is nephew, friends. Verse 16 says Zeruiah is David's sister, and Joab is her son. So David is Joab's uncle, and Joab is David's nephew. Joab ends up leading David's army (2 Samuel 8:16).
The answer is Amasa, friends. Verse 17 says, “Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.” Since Abigail is David's sister (verse 16), Amasa is another nephew of David's.

The answer is False, friends. Amnon was born by Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Daniel by Abigail of Carmel (1 Chronicles 3:1). So they have different mothers. Watch the name too: this Abigail isn't David's sister Abigail from earlier in the list. Same name, different woman.

The answer is King Talmai of Geshur, friends. Verse 2 says “…Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur…” So Absalom's grandfather on his mother's side is a king. Not a bad name to drop at a family gathering.

The answer is about forty years, friends. Verse 4 gives seven years and six months in Hebron plus thirty-three years in Jerusalem. That adds up to forty and a half. Forty and a half years on one job, which is longer than most of us stay anywhere.

The answer is Solomon, friends. Verse 5 lists Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon, and says, “These four were born to him by Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel.” Solomon's son Rehoboam then starts the next stretch in verse 10.

The answer is Tamar, friends. Verse 9 says, “And Tamar was their sister.” It's the same name as Judah's daughter-in-law from way back in chapter 2, but this one is a sister to David's sons. Two women, one name, and a list that doesn't stop to clear it up for us.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 10 starts with Solomon's son Rehoboam, then says, “Abijah was his son, Asa his son…” and keeps that up through verse 14. It's a straight father-to-son line. Like a relay race where nobody drops the baton.

The answer is Josiah, friends. Verse 14 closes the run with “Amon his son, and Josiah his son.” After that, the list moves on to Josiah's own sons in verse 15. Those four are Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum.
The answer is captive, friends. Verse 17 says “The descendants of Jeconiah the captive…” Jeremiah 24:1 tells of Jeconiah being carried away to Babylon.
The answer is False, friends. The list doesn't stop with Jeconiah. It says, “Shealtiel his son…” then moves on through Zerubbabel and keeps going until verse 24. The captive's family tree isn't done.
